name: python-package-identity
body:
A Python source file's module identity must follow Python's package model. A directory containing __init__.py or __init__.pyi is a package; a module's dotted identity is built by walking up its ancestors while they are init-bearing packages; a file with no init-bearing ancestor is a flat top-level module whose identity is its file stem (no directory qualification — this matches Python's own sys.path-top-level module semantics). The frontend emits one Module node per discovered package/module and sets each File's parent to its module, so the ingestor's `parent.name` rendering yields the dotted symbol FQNs.

The shared Module FQN namespace also carries language/package-derived names from other frontends (a Cargo package name, an npm package name, a Go module path). DECIDED (reconciled with the language-rooting decision): the rendered Python Module FQN is the language-rooted form `py.<module-identity>` — the language-namespaced form. The `py` root is disjoint from every other language's root and from markdown's rooted absolute paths, so a root Python package `apg` renders `py.apg`, never colliding with the Rust `rust.apg` module. The former open design point (bare dotted vs path-derived vs language-namespaced) is closed: requirements.note.python-frontend-open-points #1 is DECIDED. Discovery must not descend into generated/dependency trees (see domain.constraint.python-exclusions).

SCOPE / LIMITATION (reconciled with feedback-32): the `py` root removes only the CROSS-language case; it does NOT make flat init-less modules globally unique. A flat module's identity is its stem alone, so `a/foo.py` and `b/foo.py` (no __init__.py anywhere) both render `py.foo`, and the second is silently shadowed (module shadowing, src/ingest.rs:647-670). Flat init-less modules are therefore unique only WITHIN their directory. Collision-freedom is delivered for package-qualified dotted identities (globally distinct under `py`) and for flat modules whose stems are distinct; two same-stem flat modules in different directories are a known aliasing limitation, not a guarantee.

The collision hazard this guards is SILENT, not a panic: a module whose FQN is already claimed — by another module or by a type/function — is shadowed and dropped, counted in `shadowed_modules` (src/ingest.rs:647-670; logged by src/main.rs); it is not merged and it does not panic. Only a genuine same-kind Struct/Function collision fails loudly, in `claim` (src/ingest.rs:88-96). So the property to assert is 'no module in the covered identity set is silently shadowed or merged away', not merely 'no panic'.

AC: a package pkg/ with __init__.py and pkg/sub/__init__.py yields two distinct module nodes rendered `py.pkg` and `py.pkg.sub`, each containing its files' symbols; a flat-module fixture of distinct-stem init-less files in separate directories (e.g. `a/foo.py`, `b/bar.py`) yields distinct flat module nodes rendered `py.foo` and `py.bar`; across the fixture set (package-qualified identities plus distinct-stem flat modules) no two discovered modules render to the same FQN and the scan reports zero shadowed modules (`shadowed_modules` stays 0, src/ingest.rs:647-670). The fixture set must NOT contain two same-stem init-less modules in different directories: that case aliases (`py.foo` twice) and the second is expected to be shadowed under the limitation above — it is outside the collision-freedom guarantee. A same-kind symbol collision would still panic via `claim`, but that is not the module-collision hazard.
